जड

JAḌA . An immoral brahmin. jaḍa, who set out to do commercial business once was killed by thieves. As a result of sins committed in previous births he was turned into a piśāca. After his death his son, who led quite a moral life went to kāśī (Banares) to perform his father's obsequies, and at the particular spot where his father was living as piśāca the son recited Chapter 3 of the gītā, on hearing which jaḍa got released from his state as piśāca. (padma purāṇa, Uttarakhaṇḍa and mārkaṇḍeya purāṇa).
